minutes.headline: Finance Committee heard library, Council on Aging and DPW FY15 budgets; street sweeper and snow overrun dominated
minutes.summary: The committee heard FY2015 budget presentations from the library, the Council on Aging and Public Works. The DPW director warned of a large snow and ice overrun and argued for replacing a 20-year-old street sweeper, which was deferred to the capital planning discussion. The committee also approved prior minutes, discussed draft financial policies, and previewed upcoming meetings.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee heard FY2015 budget presentations from the library, the Council on Aging and Public Works; no budget was voted.
The DPW director said the department will be well over its snow and ice allotment this year.
The DPW director compared outsourcing street sweeping with buying a new sweeper; the sweeper question was deferred to the March 13 capital planning meeting.
The Council on Aging presented a budget at the town manager's recommended level, above the target, including a food services increase.
The committee approved prior minutes and discussed draft financial policies, including a proposed cap on non-exempt debt service.

why_it_matters: A snow and ice overrun has to be covered from other town funds, and a sweeper purchase would compete for capital money, so both can affect next year's tax bill and road services.
The proposed debt service cap, if adopted, would limit how much borrowing outside the tax-limit exemptions the town takes on in future years.
watch_next: March 13 capital planning meeting, where the street sweeper replacement is to be discussed.
The next revision of the fiscal policies, which a member will bring to the next meeting.
